sources.citation: Boyd, Virginia Lee. 2015. The phonological systems of the Mbam languages of Cameroon with a focus on vowels and vowel harmony. PhD dissertation, Leiden University (LOT 410). Utrecht: LOT.
sources.note: Nothing for Tuotomb: Tuotomb is explicitly excluded from the study (Intro p.2-3: 'The four languages not included in this study are Tuɔtɔmb (A46) of the village of Bonek) and Nyokon A45.. It is not included due to a lack of opportunity to collect data for it.'). Only classificatory remarks (closest to Nen lexicostatistically per Phillips 1979 and Mous & Breedveld 1986; has -VC noun-class suffixes).

sources.citation: Kerr, Elisabeth J. 2026. Auxiliaries and Analyticity in Northwestern Bantu. Nordic Journal of African Studies 35(1): 7-42. doi:10.53228/e7ym0958
sources.note: No statement about the Atɔmb tone system. The Atɔmb examples (36a-b, p. 26, own data) are transcribed with acute accents for H tone versus unmarked (L) vowels (Tám, mám, pɛ-há, káf-ak, Mɛ́, ɔ-káf) and the 1sg subject marker in (36b) is glossed 'sm.1sg:h', i.e. a grammatical H tone is segmented in the gloss - surface evidence that the fieldworker treats Atɔmb as a (two-height) tone language, but tone is neither described nor counted. Elsewhere the paper discusses tonal TAM marking in zone A languages generally (pp. 13-19), not for Atɔmb.

tone.quote: Aux-O-V order was also found in preliminary fieldwork on Atɔmb (also known as ‘Tuotomb’; A461 [ttf]), an endangered Bantu language closely related to Nyokon and spoken by <300 speakers in the village of Boneck ... While there is no published work on Atɔmb grammar, there is an unpublished PhD thesis by Dihenou Djahappi (2021). ... (36) ... a. Tám mám pɛ-há káf-ak. sm.1sg.pst prn.poss.1sg 8-thing share-dur ‘I shared my purchases.’ b. Mɛ́ naŋ ɔ-káf mám pɛ-ha. sm.1sg:h cop inf-share prn.poss.1sg 8-thing ‘I am sharing my purchases.’ (Atɔmb (A461) [ttf]; own data)
tone.locator: pp. 26-27: paragraph 'Aux-O-V order was also found in preliminary fieldwork on Atɔmb..' and fn. 9 on p. 26, ex.
